text:
maya: Heads-up — quick proposal for a canonical per-hop provenance header so hedges/retries and downstream backends can reliably know the original client identity and the multi-hop path. Sketch below.

maya: proposal: header name `x-rw-hop-provenance`. payload is a compact, ordered list of hop tokens: `client=<id>;fd=<tok>;edge=<tok>;region=<tok>`, capped and url-safe. Example: `x-rw-hop-provenance: client=acme-01;fd=fd-3;edge=east-2:a3`

sam: sg. what's the full path this intends to cover (frontdoor, regional edge, model pool)?

maya: topology: http/3 client -> frontdoor LB -> fd-edge (auth) -> regional edge proxy -> model backend (gRPC). We need this for: routing decisions, dedupe, and better telemetry when we do midstream handoffs.

rachel: we already set `x-request-id` / trace headers. how is this different?

maya: `x-request-id` is trace id (single opaque id). hop-provenance is ordered path info that is mutated by each hop. trace id stays same. provenance shows which hops touched the request and whether a resume/hedge added a new hop.

liam: concern: unbounded growth if a request is retried/hedged many times. streaming + partial resumes could append hop entries repeatedly. how do we avoid header bloat?

maya: plan: 1) cap serialized header to 512 bytes (configurable). 2) if full list won't fit, set a sentinel `truncated=true` and append a `hp-signature` (HMAC) of the canonical chain so downstreams can detect truncation without learning omitted tokens. 3) compress tokens with base62 short ids (we already assign short fd/edge tokens).

liam: HMAC good for integrity, but privacy team will ask about client id exposure. any PII concerns?

maya: agree — we should store `client` as a hash unless the customer explicitly opts into passing clear client ids. default: `client=hash:sha256(...)` and `hp-sig` signs both the hash and the chain.

devops-bot: canary note: pushed branch `hp-provenance/experiment` to staging. initial telemetry shows p50 header length 128 bytes, p99 420 bytes (without truncation).

sam: metrics we should emit: counter `hp.truncated`, histogram `hp.length.bytes`, and tag by route/model. also a gauge for `hp.malformed` when parsing fails.

rachel: operational question: when a downstream does dedupe/side-effect-protection, should it use `client` from provenance or `x-request-id`? which is canonical?

maya: proposal: `x-request-id` remains canonical trace id. For dedupe, prefer `orig-client` extracted from provenance (if present). We'll add a rule: if provenance contains `client` with clear id or verified hash signature, upstreams may treat it as the original client identity for idempotency decisions. Otherwise fall back to `x-request-id`.

liam: implementation concerns: parsing must be cheap on hot path. I'd suggest edge parse into a fixed struct (4 fields max) and expose into request context; reject overly-large headers early with 400 vs silently truncating (configurable per tenant).

maya: yep. also add a fallback header `x-rw-hop-truncated: 1` for observability to make it easier to query traces where we dropped info.

sam: can we get a small prototype and a perf microbenchmark for the hot-path parse? I'm worried about repeated base62 decode on every token.

maya: liam + maya will draft RFC and a tiny C++/rust prototype for parsing in runtime. we'll include a benchmark and the staging telemetry.

rachel: ok — sounds reasonable. please include privacy/opt-in knobs for customers.

maya: will do. owners: maya, liam. I'll open RFC+PR this week. thumbs please. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

liam: :thumbsup:

devops-bot: test run scheduled (staging) — results posted in #eng-runtime once complete.
